title: Service guardrail trigger and crediting lifecycle for dedicated tenants
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Define a single, contract-ready lifecycle that ties measured degradation events (serve-window breaches, sustained latency regressions, failed autoscale handoffs) to a deterministic crediting schedule and operational guardrails. This ticket synthesizes contract language, autoscaler interlock points, and fleet cordoning semantics so Legal, Finance, and SRE have a single reference for: 1) what counts as a breach, 2) how credits are computed and applied, and 3) what automated fleet controls (circuit cordon, prioritized queues, canary throttles) the platform may exercise before issuing credits. Deliverables: draft contract appendix, billing formula examples, ops playbook snippets, and decision matrix for when to apply automated mitigation vs immediate crediting.
acceptance_criteria: A clear definition of measurable breach events with exact metrics (tokens/min P50,P95; successful serve rate over sliding 15m window; autoscale handoff success ratio)
An error-budget-style crediting formula that can be computed from telemetry and reconciled to invoices (example computations for 1%, 5%, 20% degradation cases)
An autoscale interlock spec: enumerated trigger points, backoff windows, and deterministic timeout before crediting is eligible
An operations playbook describing automated fleet controls (cordon, priority-lane, graceful-degrade routes) and human escalation steps
Contract appendix language suitable for inclusion in a standard Dedicated Customer Agreement (plain language + technical annex)
A public-facing customer FAQ and internal runbook links included in attachments
notes: Design decision: prefer 'graceful degradation window' (GDW) as a short buffer (default 10 minutes) during which automated mitigations must be attempted before crediting begins. This balances availability vs noisy crediting.

Trade-off: smaller GDW reduces customer pain from transient spikes but increases operational churn and potential billing disputes. We recommend configurable GDW per contract tier (Standard=10m, Premium=3m, Enterprise=0m opt-in)

Credit formula draft: credit_percent = min(1.0, (observed_unserved_tokens / committed_tokens) * degradation_multiplier) where degradation_multiplier is tiered (0.8 for transient, 1.0 sustained). Convert percent to invoice credit using monthly committed spend.

Autoscale interlock: require two consecutive failed scale attempts separated by 60s to qualify as 'autoscale failure' for crediting. Failed scale attempt defined as <80% of requested additional GPU capacity accepted by runtime within 120s.

Fleet control primitives: cordon-node (stop routing new requests), priority-lane (serve existing committed clients at reduced throughput), canary-throttle (limit new session initiation to X rps). These are reversible and logged with audit IDs for billing reconciliation.
